coverage_gaps: Layer 1C remains U.S.-heavy in grid-access and utility names; region-specific policy mapping is still needed for PJM, ERCOT, SPP, MISO, CAISO, Virginia, Georgia, Illinois, Texas, Ireland, Singapore, Malaysia and China.
Need live verification of June 2026 FERC large-load action status and whether new orders changed the scoring of utilities, IPPs and grid equipment vendors.

Need direct filing checks for each company before any Layer 2 ranking: backlog, segment exposure, customer concentration, signed contracts, qualification status, capex, margin quality and regulatory treatment.
Need market-pricing checks for all high-priority names: recent relative performance, valuation expansion, short interest, earnings revisions and whether the bottleneck narrative is already crowded.
Cooling universe is likely incomplete; liquid-cooling specialists, CDU suppliers, immersion-cooling names, facility contractors and private suppliers need a dedicated node expansion.

Transformer, switchgear, cable and high-voltage equipment supplier mapping is incomplete outside Eaton, GE Vernova, Schneider, ABB, Prysmian and Nexans; need supplier-level lead-time and capacity evidence.
Advanced nuclear universe is evidence-light and speculative for several public names; needs licensing, fuel availability, customer contracts, EPC capacity and deployment milestone checks.
Water availability, permitting backlash, noise, land use, local grid-cost allocation and community resistance are underrepresented as negative chokepoints.
HBM and advanced packaging universe needs Asian-listed supplier expansion, including substrate, bonding, testing, materials and outsourced assembly/test candidates.
Global logistics and maritime chokepoint beneficiaries or victims have not been mapped into public-market candidates beyond macro evidence.

memory_update.text: The merged New Hotspots universe should prioritize bottlenecks created by AI infrastructure moving from accelerator availability toward power, interconnection, high-voltage equipment, firm generation, HBM, advanced packaging, cooling and permitting constraints.

Large-load interconnection and data-center tariff design are top-ranked chokepoint nodes because they determine whether hyperscaler demand converts into energized load, utility capex and supplier orders.

High-voltage transformers, switchgear, grid equipment, cables and EPC execution capacity should be treated as a combined grid-equipment chokepoint rather than separate generic electrical-equipment stories.
HBM and advanced packaging remain live AI compute bottlenecks, but Layer 2 must separate demand-side mega caps from scarcer supplier nodes and check whether pricing already discounts the shortage.
Firm power and nuclear-related names should be decomposed into operating nuclear generation, advanced reactor licensing, fuel availability, component suppliers, EPC capacity and grid integration.

The universe still needs dedicated Layer 1B expansions for liquid cooling, water/permitting constraints, Asian HBM/advanced-packaging suppliers, cable/transformer specialists and maritime logistics chokepoints.

Before any higher-conviction ranking, each candidate requires primary-source validation using filings, earnings calls, regulatory dockets, backlog disclosures, capex plans, customer evidence and market-pricing checks.

summary: Layer 1C merged universe for the 'New Hotspots' Serenity funnel. The highest-relevance cluster is AI infrastructure moving from pure accelerator scarcity toward power availability, grid interconnection, high-voltage equipment, firm generation, HBM/advanced packaging, cooling, and logistics chokepoints. This universe is ranked for research priority, not investment action. Scores emphasize proximity to a bottleneck, breadth across nodes, evidence strength from Layer 1A/1B cached outputs, and avoidance of an overly narrow mega-cap-only universe.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
